name: Museo Reina Sofía — Picasso's Guernica
story: Picasso painted Guernica for the Spanish Republic's pavilion at the 1937 Paris International Exhibition, in response to the bombing of the Basque town by the Condor Legion and Italian aircraft on 26 April 1937. The painting toured to raise support for the Republic. After the war it was looked after by the Museum of Modern Art in New York, which also lent it to exhibitions, because Picasso wanted it to go to Spain only when democracy returned. MoMA handed it over to the Spanish government in September 1981; it was first shown in the Casón del Buen Retiro and moved to the Reina Sofía in 1992. The surrounding rooms place it among posters, photographs and film from the war, making this the best single introduction in Madrid to the war's propaganda and art.
see: Guernica and its preparatory sketches, with rooms of Civil War posters, photographs and the 1937 pavilion material.
plan: Closed Tuesdays; free entry in the evening on most weekdays (check hours). Photos are allowed without flash, tripod or selfie stick, unless a sign in the room says otherwise. Metro Atocha.
